title: Tria capita ex opere quodam majori inedito de theoria lunae

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter 'De diametris apparentibus motuque horario vero solis ac lunae, in eclipsibus lunaribus' of Euler's posthumous lunar-theory fragment (E838). The aim is a ready-made trigonometric formula for the Moon's true hourly motion at eclipse epochs, so it need not be found by differencing two tabulated positions.

Setup from §9: u is the mean anomaly and v the eccentric anomaly of the Moon, with du = dv(1+k cos v). V is the solar anomaly, η the elongation (argument of variation), and z the Earth–Moon distance. The angular-momentum-type relation is dφ = (α − (3/2)n²M)/(z²/c²) du.

On this page Euler:
(1) Abbreviates the numerator, already evaluated numerically in §10, as α + A cos2η + B cos(2η+v) + C cos(2η−v) − D cos(2η−2v) − E cos(2η+V) − F cos(2η−V) − G cos(2η−v−V) − H cos(2η−v+V) + J cosη + K cos3η − L cos(η−v) − M cos4η + N cos v.
(2) Writes the previously found series for c/z with Fraktur coefficients 𝔄…𝔒 over the arguments v, 2v, V, v±V, η, 2η, 2η−2v, 2η−v, 2η±V, 2η−v±V.
(3) In §11 forms dφ/du = numerator·(c/z)², converts products of cosines to sums, and keeps only terms of the first and second order of smallness. The result is a column table: one column per argument, listing the contributing products. Examples:
- constant: α𝔄² + ½α𝔅² + ½α𝔥² + ½α𝔎² + A𝔄𝔥 − C𝔄𝔎;
- cos v: −2α𝔄𝔅 − α𝔅ℭ − α𝔇𝔈 + α𝔇𝔉 − A𝔄𝔎 − α𝔥𝔎 + N𝔄²;
- cos2η: 2α𝔄𝔥 + α𝔅𝔎 + A𝔄² − C𝔄𝔅;
- cos(2η−v): −2α𝔄𝔎 − α𝔅𝔥 − α𝔅𝔍 + C𝔄² − A𝔄𝔅;
- and so on through cos4η = −M𝔄² + A𝔄𝔥.
(4) In §12 substitutes numbers, with Briggs logarithms printed under each coefficient: dφ/du = 1.01188 − 0.11022 cos v + 0.004493 cos2v + 0.000242 cos V − 0.000368 cos(v+V) + 0.000358 cos(v−V) − 0.000579 cos η + 0.020356 cos2η + 0.000014 cos3η + … (continued next page).

On the next page this is multiplied by du = 1959.8″ per hour, giving 33′3″ − 216″cos v + 9″cos2v + 40″cos2η − 41″cos(2η−v) …. It is then calibrated by one comparison with the tables (1775.7″ vs 1774.7″).

Consistency checks:
- α𝔄² = 1.01188 with α = 1.0070234 gives 𝔄 ≈ 1.0024.
- 2α𝔄𝔅 = 0.11022 gives 𝔅 ≈ 0.0546, consistent with the lunar eccentricity of about 0.055.
- From cos2η: 2α𝔄𝔥 ≈ 0.020356 − 0.004662 gives 𝔥 ≈ 0.0078, the variation term in the parallax (≈ m²).
- The logarithms check: l1.01188 = 0.0051293, l0.11022 = 9.04226, l0.020356 = 8.30869, l0.000579 = 6.7627.
- 1.01188 × 1959.8″ = 1983″ = 33′3″, and 0.11022 × 1959.8 = 216″, as on the next page.
The procedure is a routine but careful product of two truncated Fourier series.
errors: Column cos(v+V): the printed '+α𝔎²' cannot contribute to cos(v+V), since 𝔎² cos²(2η−v) yields only a constant and cos(4η−2v). The correct product is −𝔎cos(2η−v)·−𝔏cos(2η+V), giving +α𝔎𝔏 (compare the analogous +α𝔎𝔐 in the cos(v−V) column). Most likely a misprint in the 1862 edition.
Column cos(2η−v+V): the printed '+α𝔅²' should be +α𝔅𝔏, from −𝔅cos v·−𝔏cos(2η+V). 𝔅² produces only a constant and cos 2v.

Column cos(2η−v+V): the term from A cos2η·2𝔄𝔉cos(v−V) is +A𝔄𝔉 if 𝔉 > 0 as written; the print has −A𝔄𝔉. Similarly, in column cos(2η−V), C cos(2η−v)·2𝔄𝔉cos(v−V) gives +C𝔄𝔉, while the print has −C𝔄𝔉. These signs are suspect unless the sign convention of 𝔉 differs. Numerically both are of order 10⁻⁶ and irrelevant to the final seconds of arc.
Column cos(2η+v): '+𝔅𝔄²' appears to be in Fraktur but should be the italic numerator coefficient B (B𝔄²); likely a typographical font error.

Several products of comparable small size are silently dropped. Examples: ½αℭ², −B𝔄𝔅 in cos2η, α𝔥𝔉/α𝔥𝔈 in the 2η−v±V columns, α𝔎𝔈/α𝔎𝔉 in the 2η±V columns. This is consistent with Euler's stated aim of keeping only terms reaching about 1″. He partly acknowledges uncertainty in §13 by empirically correcting the constant term by 1″.

ideas.what: Hourly lunar motion obtained analytically as dφ/du = (α − (3/2)n²M)(c/z)², expanded by multiplying two truncated trigonometric series and collecting arguments by product-to-sum formulas.
ideas.modern_name: Multiplication of Fourier (Poisson) series in literal perturbation theory; analytic expression for the Moon's velocity (horary motion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of 18th-century celestial mechanics (Euler, Clairaut, d'Alembert, Mayer); horary-motion tables appear in Mayer's lunar tables
ideas.where_published: Same technique throughout Euler's lunar theories, e.g. Theoria motus lunae (E187, 1753) and Theoria motuum lunae (E418, 1772); the specific eclipse-oriented horary formula appears only in this posthumous piece as far as I know

ideas.what: Use of the lunar eccentric anomaly v as the independent variable, with du = dv(1+k cos v), mixed with the elongation η and solar anomaly V as arguments.
ideas.modern_name: Eccentric-anomaly formulation of lunar theory (cf. Hansen's later methods)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hansen (19th c.) for systematic lunar theory in eccentric-type anomalies; Euler used such variables earlier
ideas.where_published: Probably in Euler's lunar-theory manuscripts and partly E418; unsure of precise published locus

ideas.what: Logarithmic bookkeeping of each coefficient (Briggs logs printed beneath) to facilitate multiplication by l du = 3.292212.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, carefully organised algebraic–numerical step in Euler's lunar theory: the product of two Fourier series to get the horary motion for eclipse computations. The only noteworthy items are a few apparent misprints or sign slips in the coefficient table (α𝔎² for α𝔎𝔏, α𝔅² for α𝔅𝔏, signs of A𝔄𝔉 and C𝔄𝔉), all numerically negligible. Nothing conceptually new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: 'sitque brevitatis gr[?]' – text is cut off at the page edge; reads 'brevitatis gratia'.
First line of the c/z series ends with '+ 𝔥 cos 2η' (partly cut off at margin); line 2 ends '+ 𝔑 cos(2η − v + V)' (cut off).
First line of §11 ends '+2α𝔄𝔉 cos(v − V)' (cut off at margin).
In §11 the material is a column table, not running rows. Constant column: α𝔄², +½α𝔅², +½α𝔥², +½α𝔎², +A𝔄𝔥, −C𝔄𝔎.
The machine transcription scrambles the column assignments of the rows above.
Column cos(η − v): +α𝔅𝔊 cos(η − v), −L𝔄² (the argument is cut off at the margin).
Last column of the fourth block is '+2α𝔄𝔒 cos(2η − v − V)' (cut off).
Final block: '+B𝔄²' in the cos(2η+v) column – the print shows a Fraktur-looking 𝔅 but italic B is meant.
§12: '−0,000368 cos(v+V)' is partly cut off at the right margin.
